details:
Can we consider Whitelisting for Quest Avatars and Worlds "URP"?
Universal Render Pipeline (or URP for short, formerly LWRP or Light Weight Render Pipeline) is one of the render pipelines available in Unity. It offers varieties of post-processing effects and lighting configurations while maintaining high performance.
The built in rendering software is not only buggy, but it hinders me personally from creating bigger worlds. 
This is very important because when you are creating bigger prefabs and worlds, the materials and shaders are taking up lots of processing power and by converting to URP you can see a massive overhaul.
This would be a feature I would like to see added to the Engine you are running for your game platform. It would be absolutely astounding to get more out of the VR experience as well. 
If the rendering program is already enabled, let me know and I will gladly start converting my small projects.
Unfortunately, we do not live in 2019 anymore and I know that there is some nostalgia with using older versions of Unity. 
However, time moves forward and the good news is that there is no reason to to go to a new unity variant. This feature I am asking for is one that is used in all versions and is "verified", so it can be used in commercial products. 
VR is a cutting edge area, and being able to use tech that would make building things better for all users, including being able to use industry standard tools. There is really no downside. 
I know I am pushing this hard, so I will tell you its drawbacks. Unfortunately, there is a catch when using URP. It will change the default shaders from standard to a URP variant. Now that is great because then the projects move forward with more optimized and performance boosted materials. However, I am not sure what kind of drawback that would have on the current setups you have.
I am an aspiring world builder and I do like to see performance. 
Here is an example video that will easily show you how much of a difference in performance and optimization that can be accomplished through this switch. It even is in version 19.3.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HqaQJfuK_u8
Rumor: "Unity will eventually drop support for builtin and URP is faster across the board than builtin. In fact, Unity considers it a bug if URP is ever slower and will fix it pronto so it isn't"
Topic: https://forum.unity.com/threads/urp-vs-standard-render.852004/
This is a quote from a VR developer:
"I am a VR developer, on Quest and up.
You can still use builtin's shaders providing they have custom lighting (vert/frag not surface). You can also see that FFR has been unavailable in Unity and it's actually Oculus' responsibly to implement this.
Likely, the people complaining have been using lighter shaders and not using an equivalent on the URP side, and invoking the Oculus library's FFR.
In any case I've tried game scenes with URP lit set to 4 lights without FFR. The Quest did not drop frames.
So I think otherwise. "
